newsitem.title: POLAND: LG Group says plans $2.5 bln E.Europe investment.
newsitem.headline: LG Group says plans $2.5 bln E.Europe investment.

text.p: South Korea's LG Group plans to invest $2.5 billion in Europe by the year 2000, concentating on countries former Soviet Union countries and Poland, its officials said on Thursday.

At its annual strategy meeting held in Warsaw LG Group officials said the concern would invest $1.5 billion in the former Soviet Union, $700 million in Poland and $100 million in Bulgaria by the end of the century.
"LG Group will invest $2.5 billion in this region (Europe) by the year 2000," deputy president Dze Kop Sung told a news conference at the end of the first day of the annual meeting.
LG Group's managing director of global operations Chong Suk Li added Russia will be the centre of the Korean firm's future investments.

"Russia is the focus for our future investment endeavours in excavation of natural resources and construction," Chong Suk Li said, adding that $400 million would be invested in excavation of hard coal alone.
More than half of LG Group's total $1.2 billion investment in Central Europe will be placed in Poland, mostly in the electronic, construction, telecommunications and chemical sectors.
"In Poland we would like to enter sectors such as semi-conductors, telecommunications, construction as well as the financial arena," Chong Suk Li said.
"In the electronics sector, LG Group is planning several investments... We are interested in production of colour television sets," he added.
LG Group will invest $100 million in cellular telephone products and about $400 million in construction in Poland.
In June, the Korean concern bought a controling stake in Petrobank SA, a small Polish bank, for nearly $50 million.
Chong Suk Li said LG Group would invest $100 million to set up a soda production plant in Bulgaria by the end of the century. He gave no other details about the investment in the Balkan country.
LG Group revenues totalled $64.3 billion in 1995, up from $39 billion in 1994. Last year its net profit rose to $1.7 billion from just under one billion in 1994.
Chong Suk Li said LG Group planned to raise its annual revenue to $385 billion by 2005 through its investment scheme.
"We want to increase our annual revenue to about $385 billion in 2005 and be a local yet truly global firm," he said.
